    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>Steam updated their login UI a little while back and made it worse with more annoyances, but there was still a way to use the old login UI. All one would have to do was add "-noreactlogin" to the Target in the shortcut properties. That's not working anymore. So, how do I use the old Login UI as of February 3rd, 2023?</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<p>Steam updated their login UI a little while back and made it worse with more annoyances, but there was still a way to use the old login UI. All one would have to do was add "-noreactlogin" to the Target in the shortcut properties. That's not working anymore. So, how do I use the old Login UI as of February 3rd, 2023?</p>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>This is a Loyalty Rank 12 feature of the <a href="https://www.arcgames.com/en/games/neverwinter/news/detail/9492533-neverwinter%3A-introducing-the-vip-program!" rel="nofollow noreferrer">VIP Program</a> — meaning that it is only accessible after you have paid for 12 months of VIP access.  (By purchasing <a href="https://neverwinter.fandom.com/wiki/VIP_Program" rel="nofollow noreferrer">VIP Packs</a> from the Zen Store.)</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Summon banking portal: ability to use personal bank from anywhere. Anyone around will be able to use the bank.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>So, yes, you can buy them.  The currency required is Zen, which you can acquire for Real World Money, or for Astral Diamonds on the Exchange (<em>lots</em> of Astral Diamonds — up to 750 per Zen), and it lasts for as long as your VIP status does.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>This is a Loyalty Rank 12 feature of the <a href="https://www.arcgames.com/en/games/neverwinter/news/detail/9492533-neverwinter%3A-introducing-the-vip-program!" rel="nofollow noreferrer">VIP Program</a> — meaning that it is only accessible after you have paid for 12 months of VIP access.  (By purchasing <a href="https://neverwinter.fandom.com/wiki/VIP_Program" rel="nofollow noreferrer">VIP Packs</a> from the Zen Store.)</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Summon banking portal: ability to use personal bank from anywhere. Anyone around will be able to use the bank.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>So, yes, you can buy them.  The currency required is Zen, which you can acquire for Real World Money, or for Astral Diamonds on the Exchange (<em>lots</em> of Astral Diamonds — up to 750 per Zen), and it lasts for as long as your VIP status does.</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>This is a Loyalty Rank 12 feature of the <a href="https://www.arcgames.com/en/games/neverwinter/news/detail/9492533-neverwinter%3A-introducing-the-vip-program!" rel="nofollow noreferrer">VIP Program</a> — meaning that it is only accessible after you have paid for 12 months of VIP access.  (By purchasing <a href="https://neverwinter.fandom.com/wiki/VIP_Program" rel="nofollow noreferrer">VIP Packs</a> from the Zen Store.)</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Summon banking portal: ability to use personal bank from anywhere. Anyone around will be able to use the bank.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>So, yes, you can buy them.  The currency required is Zen, which you can acquire for Real World Money, or for Astral Diamonds on the Exchange (<em>lots</em> of Astral Diamonds — up to 750 per Zen), and it lasts for as long as your VIP status does.</p>
</div>

    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401540/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401558/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="post-layout">

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401558/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401558/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I am playing the Japanese version of Hogwarts Legacy on PC (Steam). The store page says that Hogwarts Legacy has Full Audio support for 8 languages, including Japanese.</p>
<p>But, for immersion, I want to play in the language of the country in which it is set, for example, in this case, the UK, and I would like to try to play in the audio of that language, if available.</p>
<p>According to the <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/990080/Hogwarts_Legacy/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">store page</a>, of course it includes English Full Audio support - however, I cannot find a way to change the audio language in my game. There seems to be no setting in the settings either.</p>
<p>Is there any way to change the audio language to a specific language, in this case, English?</p>
</div>

<div class="post-layout">

<a aria-label="Timeline" class="js-post-issue flex--item s-btn s-btn__unset c-pointer py6 mx-auto" data-controller="s-tooltip" data-ks-title="timeline" data-s-tooltip-placement="right" data-shortcut="T" href="/posts/401558/timeline" title="Show activity on this post."><svg aria-hidden="true" class="mln2 mr0 svg-icon iconHistory" height="18" viewbox="0 0 19 18" width="19"><path d="M3 9a8 8 0 1 1 3.73 6.77L8.2 14.3A6 6 0 1 0 5 9l3.01-.01-4 4-4-4h3L3 9Zm7-4h1.01L11 9.36l3.22 2.1-.6.93L10 10V5Z"></path></svg></a>

<div class="answercell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>I've found a way, apparently:</p>
<p>According to <a href="https://steamcommunity.com/app/990080/discussions/0/3761104682791235953/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">this post</a> on Steam community, you can edit your .exe of Hogwarts Legacy to get English VO with (possbily) your favorite supported language's subtitles.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Steam\steamapps\common\Hogwarts Legacy\Phoenix\Binaries\Win64</p>
<p>↑Open HogwartsLegacy.exe in the location shown above with a binary editor.</p>
<p>Search for "zh-CN" in the binary editor</p>
<p>Change "zh-CN" to "ja-JP" and "schinece" to "japanese" and save</p>
<p>Change the language to Simplified Chinese from the Hogwarts Legacy properties on Steam</p>
<p>Launch the game.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>(quoted that post, edited a little to look better on stackexchange)</p>
<p>I guess this method is "abusing" a language that has no Full Audio support (zh-CN is Simplified Chinese (schinese), and that language doesn't have Full Audio support; I think default VO is English, so any language that has no Full Audio support, the VO will be English and subtitles will be the language player have chosen) to have English VO, and your desired supported language's subtitles.</p>
<p>Below is a list of country codes that has Full Audio support, if I'm not mistaken (excluded English):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>fr-FR</code> <code>french</code></li>
<li><code>it-IT</code> <code>italian</code></li>
<li><code>de-DE</code> <code>german</code></li>
<li><code>es-ES</code> <code>spanish</code></li>
<li><code>ja-JP</code> <code>japanese</code></li>
<li><code>pt-BR</code> <code>brazilian</code></li>
<li><code>es-MX</code> <code>latam</code></li>
</ul>
<p>Simply change <code>zh-CN</code> and <code>schinese</code> to your favorite language (if French, <code>fr-FR</code> and <code>french</code>) to get English VO/French subtitles. Though, I haven't tested myself other than Japanese, so I don't know if it actually works.</p>
<p>Use your favorite Hex Editor to achieve it. I've used <a href="https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/" rel="nofollow noreferrer">HxD</a>, but anything that can edit .exe should work.</p>
<p>Disclaimer: I don't know if this method will lead you get banned, but knowing that this game is single-player only, I don't think it'll lead you to ban, but I do not take any responsibility.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In the old Ace Ventura Action Adventure from 1995 you have to build a pile of 6 pieces in the right order, out of 8 pieces.</p>
<p>There are 20.160 different combinations. It turns out that this is the right one:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/x0e0v.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/x0e0v.png"/></a></p>
<p>I found the solution using Google, but without explanation. How are you supposed to find the right combination? Building a combination together with a short animation takes at least 10s, so it's just impossible to simply try out all combinations.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In the old Ace Ventura Action Adventure from 1995 you have to build a pile of 6 pieces in the right order, out of 8 pieces.</p>
<p>There are 20.160 different combinations. It turns out that this is the right one:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/x0e0v.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/x0e0v.png"/></a></p>
<p>I found the solution using Google, but without explanation. How are you supposed to find the right combination? Building a combination together with a short animation takes at least 10s, so it's just impossible to simply try out all combinations.</p>
</div>

<script>
    StackExchange.ready(function () {
        StackExchange.Hero.init("nso", "a");

        var location = 0;
        if ($("body").hasClass("questions-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("question-page")) {
            location = 1;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("faq-page")) {
            location = 5;
        } else if ($("body").hasClass("home-page")) {
            location = 3;
        }

        $('.js-cta-button').click(function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: 'cta', location: location }, true);
            });
        });

        // TODO: we should review the class names and whatnot in use here. Older heroes use id selectors, the newer
        // sticky question hero on SO has a .js-dismiss class instead, but it's apparently not used anywhere... 
        // It's not great. Ideally we'd have a set of classes in the partials above that would correspond to 
        // the behaviours we want here in a more clear way. 

        // sticky question-page hero at the bottom of the page on SO
        $('.js-dismiss').on('click', function () {
            StackExchange.using("gps", function () {
                StackExchange.gps.track("hero.action", { hero_action_type: "close", location: location }, true);
            });
            StackExchange.Hero.dismiss();
            $(".js-dismissable-hero").fadeOut("fast");
        });
    });
</script>

<div class="postcell post-layout--right">
<div class="s-prose js-post-body" itemprop="text">
<p>In the old Ace Ventura Action Adventure from 1995 you have to build a pile of 6 pieces in the right order, out of 8 pieces.</p>
<p>There are 20.160 different combinations. It turns out that this is the right one:</p>
<p><a href="https://i.stack.imgur.com/x0e0v.png" rel="nofollow noreferrer"><img alt="enter image description here" src="https://i.stack.imgur.com/x0e0v.png"/></a></p>
<p>I found the solution using Google, but without explanation. How are you supposed to find the right combination? Building a combination together with a short animation takes at least 10s, so it's just impossible to simply try out all combinations.</p>
</div>
